summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a relative path.
description: `nonRelative(value)` is the same test as `!isRelative(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The exact complement of `isAbsolute`: anything that does not start at a root, which includes the empty string.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a relative path; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonRelative("/var/log"); // => true
nonRelative("https://example.com/a"); // => true
nonRelative("docs/readme.md"); // => false
nonRelative("./a"); // => false
nonRelative(""); // => false
```
